items.titel: Mercedes-Benz halts new investment in German plants, considers closures
items.anriss: The Stuttgart carmaker is temporarily halting all further investment at its German sites. Possible plant closures are looming, increasing pressure on staff, works council and IG Metall. Volkswagen and Audi have also announced major savings …

absaetze.t: Published on 12 November 2026 - 20:22 GMT+1•Updated 21:33

The future of Mercedes-Benz's production sites in Germany is coming under increasing pressure. Because of high labour costs and stalled talks with the works council and IG Metall, the Stuttgart carmaker is taking action. The management board has decided to suspend all further investment at German sites for the time being. Possible plant closures are now also being considered in more concrete terms.
ADVERTISEMENT
Mercedes puts the brakes on spending

As bild.de reported on Thursday, HR director Britta Seeger justified the move by pointing to the strained cost situation. The group now has to examine which locations in Germany can still be operated profitably in the long term. Mercedes wants to avoid plant closures as far as possible, she said, but this option now has to be pursued more seriously than before.

The talks with employee representatives are considered deadlocked. A swift agreement is currently not in sight, Seeger explained in an internal interview that zeit.de reported on, citing the news agency Reuters. The aim remains a joint package that delivers noticeable savings while at the same time being socially acceptable.

At the heart of the dispute are production costs. According to Mercedes, an hour of labour in German plants can cost up to five times as much as at sites in Eastern Europe. The management board is therefore demanding concessions on working conditions. One proposal under discussion is to extend working hours without increasing pay.
Special payments such as profit sharing, holiday bonuses and Christmas bonuses could also be subject to cuts. The demands have already triggered protests among employees.
Sindelfingen, Rastatt or Bremen?

Head of production Michael Schiebe had already announced a few weeks ago that if cost reductions fail to materialise, two plants in Germany could be closed. Under current thinking, this would affect one vehicle assembly plant and one so called powertrain plant where vehicle components are manufactured.

According to zeit.de, Mercedes operates assembly plants among other places in Sindelfingen, Rastatt and Bremen. Powertrain sites include Stuttgart-Untertürkheim, Affalterbach, Berlin, Hamburg and Kamenz as well as locations in Thuringia. It is not yet known which specific plants could be affected by possible closures.
Volkswagen and subsidiary Audi are also cutting costs
The cost cutting is seen as driven not only by high site costs but also by the group's economic difficulties. In recent years Mercedes-Benz has struggled with falling sales and slumping profits.
The problems are not limited to the Stuttgart manufacturer. Volkswagen and Audi have also announced extensive savings programmes and job cuts.

Automotive expert Ferdinand Dudenhöffer sees these developments, according to bild.de, as a consequence of the long known competitiveness problems of Germany as a car manufacturing location. Without a fundamental change in cost structures, he warns, Germany's car industry risks losing even more of its competitiveness.

The dispute at Mercedes thus highlights the growing pressure on the German car industry. While the company is pushing for lower production costs, the works council and IG Metall are trying to safeguard jobs and collectively agreed benefits. An agreement is still not in sight.

items.titel: L-39NG Skyfox Jets Could Give Ukraine A Critical New Russian Drone Hunting Capability
items.anriss: The Czech Republic could supply Ukraine with up to 16 Aero L-39NG Skyfox aircraft, potentially giving Kyiv another option for countering Russia’s Shahed-type attack drones . The proposal includes four aircraft previously agreed for …

absaetze.t: The Czech Republic could supply Ukraine with up to 16 Aero L-39NG Skyfox aircraft, potentially giving Kyiv another option for countering Russia’s Shahed-type attack drones. The proposal includes four aircraft previously agreed to for transfer and 12 more that Czech officials are now discussing with their Ukrainian counterparts.

Czech Deputy Prime Minister and Industry and Trade Minister Karel Havlíček raised the expanded arrangement during a visit to Kyiv yesterday, where he met Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhiy Koretskyi. Havlíček described the discussions as encouraging but did not announce a finalized agreement for the additional aircraft.

Skyfox is based on the Cold War-era Aero L-39 Albatros jet trainer, a rugged and reliable Soviet aircraft that was produced in the thousands and served all over the globe. The new L-39NG was reworked and modernized in the 2010s in an effort to recapture jet trainer market share that had waned as the Soviet design was increasingly passed over for more modern alternatives. Many L-39s are also flown privately in the United States and are used for contracted air support services for the U.S. military. One of the firms that uses them, Draken International, actually assisted in the L-39NG project and acted as a U.S. anchor for the program.

The Skyfox’s redesigned structure makes use of modern materials, reducing weight and increasing structural lifespan to 15,000 flight hours. The American Williams FJ44-4M turbofan, a very widely used jet engine that is found on many private jets, replaces the original Soviet-designed engine, offering far better fuel efficiency, digital engine control, updated ejection seats and improved maintenance support. In contrast to the old Albatros, the Skyfox has a modern glass cockpit and an updated flight control system. The Skyfox has a maximum speed of approximately 560 miles per hour, a service ceiling of 38,000 feet, and five external hardpoints for carrying weapons and other mission equipment. Like its predecessor, although primarily a jet trainer, it also has light combat capabilities.

Its potential counter-drone role is tied to Aero Vodochody’s Drone Hunter concept, which is being developed specifically to engage uncrewed aerial vehicles. The proposed L-39NG configuration features an electro-optical targeting system and launchers for 70mm laser-guided rockets. Gun pods would be another potential option for the counter-drone role.

Drone Hunter would provide Ukraine with a reliable airborne platform for rapidly engaging attack drones, reducing reliance on more expensive surface-to-air missiles and conventional fighter aircraft. However, the system has not yet entered operational service, and its effectiveness will depend on the results of further testing and integration work. Aero Vodochody is working with Belgian defense company Thales on the guided rocket system.

A dedicated counter-drone aircraft in this class would also help preserve Ukraine’s more capable fighter fleet for other missions. Its F-16s, along with the country’s remaining MiG-29 Fulcrums, Su-27 Flankers, and French-supplied Mirage 2000s, are needed for a much wider range of tasks, including counter-air operations, air-to-ground strikes, and intercepting more challenging Russian cruise missiles and jet-powered one-way attack drones. Using these aircraft extensively to hunt relatively inexpensive and slower one-way attack drones adds flight hours, increases maintenance demands, and consumes finite stocks of air-to-air weapons.

Ukraine’s F-16 fleet is already under considerable strain. As TWZ recently reported, more than half of the aircraft were reportedly stuck in maintenance limbo, while shortages of AIM-9 Sidewinder and AIM-120 AMRAAM missiles were further complicating operations. The fighters have also been increasingly tasked with countering Russia’s expanding use of faster, jet-powered attack drones. A separate aircraft optimized for engaging slower uncrewed targets could help ease some of that burden.

The potential economic advantage is also significant. Laser-guided 70mm rockets are a much less expensive means of engaging drones compared to conventional air-to-air missiles. Already, Ukraine appears to have introduced the U.S.-made 70mm Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System II (APKWS II) rockets to the arsenal available for its F-16s. The Thales 70mm laser-guided rocket is very similar, as you can read about here, and is already being employed by Ukraine in ground-based applications.
As we have reported in the past, guided rockets offer clear cost advantages over traditional air-to-air missiles:

Each APKWS II consists of three core components: a 70mm rocket motor, one of several standard warhead options, and a guidance and control section in between. The guidance and control element is by far the most costly of the three, with a unit price of around $15,000. The warhead and motor add another few thousand dollars to the total cost, which is generally in the $20,000 to $25,000 range. By comparison, current-generation variants of the AIM-120 are in the $1 million unit cost range, with the latest versions of the AIM-9X also being priced at around $500,000.
Aside from the effectors, operating the Skyfox is an entirely different cost proposition than the F-16, for example.

Aero Vodochody puts the Skyfox’s operating costs at approximately $1,700 to $2,300 per flight hour, compared with around $22,000 for an F-16-class fighter. The Skyfox also requires a much less demanding maintenance and logistical support footprint than a frontline fighter. It can fly from rough strips and roadways with ease and can be more readily hidden from view due to its small size.
Ukraine has also previously shown that it is more than willing to adopt less-conventional aerial platforms for countering the drone menace.

One notable example is the Antonov An-28 twin-engine turboprop utility aircraft that has been adapted into a Shahed hunter. The aircraft has been equipped with M134 Miniguns and, more recently, underwing launchers for Ukrainian-made interceptor drones. This approach allows the aircraft to act as an airborne launch platform, bringing interceptors closer to incoming threats while using its own sensors and crew to help locate them. The An-28’s relatively long endurance and short takeoff and landing capabilities also make it well suited to sustained patrols from austere airfields.
The Skyfox would offer a different approach, using a jet-powered platform and guided rockets and gun pods rather than relying on trainable guns or air-launched interceptor drones.

In terms of crewed aircraft being used or considered for counter-drone missions, the L-39NG Skyfox would occupy something of a middle ground. At the higher end are aircraft like the F-16 and other combat jets, which offer substantially greater performance and broader combat capabilities but are also more valuable assets that require much greater levels of support. At the lower end are platforms such as the An-28, helicopters, and even repurposed propeller-driven training aircraft, which offer relatively inexpensive ways to patrol for and engage slower-moving drones.

The requirement for additional counter-drone capabilities is becoming more pressing as Russia continues to evolve its Shahed-family weapons. Alongside the familiar propeller-driven Geran-2, which was derived from the Iranian Shahed-136, Moscow has increasingly employed jet-powered variants, including the Geran-3 and newer Geran-4 and Geran-5. These drones fly faster and at higher altitudes, making them significantly more challenging to engage with the relatively inexpensive interceptor drones Ukraine has relied on heavily.

The Geran-4, for example, is reported to reach speeds of around 280 to 310 miles per hour and operate at altitudes of up to 26,000 feet. Newer variants are also incorporating improved navigation, cameras, and communications equipment, potentially allowing for greater autonomy and more flexible targeting. Russia’s growing use of these weapons is placing additional pressure on Ukraine’s already stretched air-defense network.

Speaking to TWZ, Justin Bronk, Senior Research Fellow for Airpower and Military Technology at RUSI, noted that the L-39NG “offers an unusually attractive combination of attributes as a dedicated counter-drone interceptor; being fast enough to easily intercept Geran-3 and Geran-4 jet-powered drones, very cheap and simple to operate compared to frontline fighters and even other advanced trainer jets, already having targeting pod, gunpod and rocket pod options integrated, and being available quickly due to a small existing order book.”
“It also has impressive endurance for an aircraft of its size and weight, so it can stay on station longer than most other jet options without air-to-air refuelling,” Bronk added.
This is largely thanks to its FJ44 engine and is critical to being able to rapidly respond to new inbound threats while remaining airborne for extended periods during raids.

However, Bronk also pointed to its primary limitation: having a radar. “While this makes it harder to acquire the drones during an intercept, it is not as problematic in Ukraine given the extensive existing network of radar-equipped ground-control stations to help guide interceptors to the rough vicinity of the target,” he said.

In addition, Ukraine already has large numbers of pilots and maintenance personnel who are familiar with the previous-generation L-39, so training should be very straightforward to operate the L-39NG. Ukraine’s L-39s have even flown combat operations during the war.

The new Czech proposal follows Ukraine’s unsuccessful effort to obtain L-159 ALCA light combat aircraft from Prague. Czech President Petr Pavel previously supported transferring some of the aircraft to Kyiv, and the Czech military indicated it could release up to four. However, Prime Minister Andrej Babiš’s government rejected the proposal, arguing that the aircraft were needed by the Czech Armed Forces.

The L-159 has a radar, the Italian FIAR Grifo L, which was eyed as a highly beneficial tool for crews independently detecting and engaging inbound drones, even in all weather conditions. But as Bronk explained, this can be overcome to a degree thanks to Ukraine’s vast drone detection and tracking network.
Already in service with the Czech Republic, Hungary, and Vietnam, the Skyfox is also on order for Angola and Armenia.

Aero Vodochody currently produces approximately 12 Skyfox aircraft annually, with the potential to increase output to 18. However, the company’s production schedule was reportedly booked through the second quarter of 2027, potentially complicating deliveries to Ukraine.

Whatever happens next, the development is indicative of how drone-hunting aircraft are increasingly becoming a feature of the evolving air defense landscape, as militaries look for more economical ways to counter the proliferation of one-way attack drones. It also highlights the possibility that other trainer types could be used to help reduce costs and save the higher-end fighters for more complex missions. Such a strategy could become more widely adopted globally as the threat of one-way attack drones continues to metastasize.

items.titel: La Marine nationale va créer huit escouades de réserve côtières de plus en 2027

absaetze.t: On en compte actuellement dix-neuf… Et elles seront bientôt vingt-sept. En effet, ce 12 novembre, le ministère des Armées a annoncé que la Marine nationale allait former huit escouades de réserve côtières [ECR] de plus dans le courant de l’année prochaine.

Pour rappel, en 2023, considérant qu’il fallait «durcir» la défense maritime en comblant les «angles morts» de cette dernière, la Marine nationale avait fait part de son intention de créer des «flottilles côtières» pour les façades littorales de l’Atlantique, de la Méditerranée et de la Manche-Mer du Nord.

Chacune d’entre-elles devait s’appuyer sur un état-major et compter dix escouades dotées de moyens nautiques [des semi-rigides Sillinger 765 Proraid] mis en œuvre par soixante-dix marins réservistes. Et il était aussi question de créer six autres escouades dans les outre-mer.

«L’objectif est de constituer des moyens de surveillance nautique qui seront armés par des réservistes, à la fois anciens et jeunes. Ces derniers navigueront sur des embarcations à coque semi-rigide et patrouilleront en lien avec les sémaphores dans des missions d’assistance publique et de renseignement», avai expliqué l’amiral Pierre Vandier, alors chef d’état-major de la Marine nationale.

Quoi qu’il en soit, selon les décisions que vient de valider Catherine Vautrin, la ministre des Armées, deux nouvelles escouades seront créées à Lézardrieux [Côtes-d’Armor] et à Royan [Charente-Maritime]. Elles relèveront donc de l’état-major implanté à Brest.

S’agissant de la façade Manche-mer du Nord, trois escouades verront le jour à Dieppe [Seine-Maritime], à Granville [Manche] et à Ouistreham [Calvados]. «Elles intégreront la flottille de réserve côtière Manche-mer du Nord basée à Cherbourg-en-Cotentin qui comprend déjà les escouades de Dunkerque et du Havre», a précisé le ministère.

Enfin, trois autres escouades de réserve côtière verront le jour à La Ciotat [Bouches-du-Rhône], à Saint-Raphaël [Var] et à Gruissan [Aude] et, partant, intégreront la flottille de réserve côtière Méditerranée basée à Toulon.

Quand le dispositif sera totalement déployé, d’ici 2030, «les flottilles et escouades de réserve côtières emploieront environ 3 000 réservistes opérationnels et seront équipées de vecteurs nautiques, routiers, et aériens, ces derniers prenant la forme de micro-drones», a souligné le ministère des Armées.

Et d’ajouter que ces unités de réservistes «complètent l’actuel dispositif en profondeur de surveillance générale des approches maritimes» et qu’elles «sont employées dans un cadre d’action intégré, comprenant à la fois des missions militaires de Défense maritime du territoire et d’action de l’État en mer».

Lors de sa première audition à l’Assemblée nationale, l’actuel CEMM, l’amiral Christophe Cluzel avait indiqué que la Marine nationale comptait environ 7 000 réservistes et que l’objectif est de porter leur nombre à 18 000 d’ici 2035.

«Les moyens financiers nécessaires sont prévus afin de soutenir cette progression. Cette montée en puissance est d’ailleurs relativement simple à mettre en œuvre grâce à la création des flottilles de réserve maritime. Celles-ci nous ont permis de recruter ce que nous appelons des réservistes ab initio, avec des résultats particulièrement remarquables», avait-il dit.

items.titel: « Tout est simple, presque pauvre » : les toiles envoûtantes de Yu Nishimura à savourer dans une exposition gratuite à Paris
items.anriss: Des poissons anodins flottent dans une eau iridescente ( School of Fish , 2021), un homme regarde par la fenêtre des oiseaux voler ( Open the window , 2022), une figure agenouillée ramasse des coquillages sur la plage ( Low Tide , 2024) : …

absaetze.t: Virtuoses, les peintures silencieuses du Japonais sacrent la fragilité des choses ordinaires et la splendide impermanence du monde.

Des poissons anodins flottent dans une eau iridescente (School of Fish, 2021), un homme regarde par la fenêtre des oiseaux voler (Open the window, 2022), une figure agenouillée ramasse des coquillages sur la plage (Low Tide, 2024) : tout est simple, presque pauvre. Yu Nishimura, né en 1982 au Japon, scrute les rituels ordinaires et le parti pris des choses, saisit des instants décisifs, car enfuis, élabore « des scènes qui échappent à toute désignation précise », à la manière d’Alex Katz. Un travail à découvrir dans le cadre d’une exposition gratuite à Lafayette Anticipations, jusqu’au 3 janvier 2027.
Une mémoire vibrante de l’instant

Diplômé en 2004 de la Tama Art University, le jeune homme s’enthousiasme pour la peinture de Luc Tuymans et de Yoshitomo Nara, sait dissimuler sous des dehors naïfs une dextérité sans faille, de même que les hérauts de l’écriture plate. À ceci près que Nishimura ne renonce pas aux effets de style, qui lui permettent de faire vibrer des formes instables à la manière des écrans réverbérants, des affichages rétroéclairés et des vidéos pré-numériques, tous ces supports hypnotiques de la « décennie perdue ». À On Kawara et Giorgio Morandi, Nishimura emprunte le désir de fixer « l’atmosphère d’un jour donné » et, à l’huile, superpose sur la surface de la toile des persistances rétiniennes, celles que la mémoire dépose sur l’œil et dans l’esprit.
Yu Nishimura, Low tide, 2024, huile sur toile, 194 x 130 cm ©Kei Okano.

Ces merveilleuses surimpressions, qui peuplent les plus grandes institutions internationales, de la Collection Pinault au LACMA de Los Angeles, sont des haïkus vifs comme l’éclat et comme la foudre, quand « coexistent la lumière et l’obscurité ». Rien ne semble pouvoir détourner le geste de l’artiste, qui travaille depuis toujours où il est né, entouré de ses enfants et de son épouse – la peintre Ulala Imai. Et si la beauté a partie liée avec la distance ou le retrait, alors Yu Nishimura fait des œuvres belles.
Yu Nishimura, Behind Branches,2025, huile sur toile, 15,8 x 22,7 cm ©Kei Okano.
Yu Nishimura en bref
1982 Naissance de Yu Nishimura à Kanagawa, au Japon.
2004 Diplôme de la Tama Art University de Tokyo, en peinture à l’huile.
2009 Participation à la 6e triennale de peinture du Kiyosu City Haruhi Art Museum, à Aichi, au Japon.
2017 Lauréat du Grand Prix Kijo Kinutani.
2020 « Scenes of beholder », première exposition personnelle, à la galerie Crèvecœur, Paris.
2024 Intégration de la photographie dans son travail. Acquisition par le Centre Pompidou de sa peinture Boy (2023).
2025 « Clearing Unfolds », première exposition à la galerie David Zwirner, à New York.

items.titel: Crosslam completes Brazil's tallest mass-timber tower
items.anriss: Engineering company Crosslam has designed and built Aurora 275, a hybrid building with mass-timber elements that the company claims is the tallest of its type in Brazil .

absaetze.t: Engineering company Crosslam has designed and built Aurora 275, a hybrid building with mass-timber elements that the company claims is the tallest of its type in Brazil.

Standing 22 metres tall, Aurora 275 is considered a hybrid-timber building, with a structural system consisting of a reinforced concrete core, metal, and mass-timber elements including glued-laminated timber (glulam) beams and columns.
Located in the Suzano area of São Paulo, according to Crosslam, it is the tallest building of its type in Brazil.
Crosslam, which usually acts as an engineer for other firms, designed the building itself to demonstrate the potential of mass timber in Brazil.
“We believed that, to sell the first timber building, we first had to build our own,” said Crosslam founder José Alberto Corrêa. “Otherwise, the Brazilian market wouldn’t trust that it was possible.”

To further demonstrate the method’s viability, the building was constructed in four weeks by a five-person team, according to Crosslam. The timber was produced in the company’s factory using wood sourced from Brazil.
Aurora 275 sits next to smaller residential buildings. It features a metal-clad facade, with yellow detailing running up its face.
It extends in two directions from a concrete core, with balconies for each of the 10 apartments.
On the outside, the timber elements are only visible on the undersides of the balconies.
However, on the inside, the timber elements are more visible, with the cross-laminated timber floorplates and glulam beams exposed, giving the interiors a warm feel.
Crosslam said that the structure shows the potential for timber buildings for industrial-style housing production in the country.
“Using engineered timber offers benefits related to the industrialisation of construction, the efficiency of the assembly process, and building performance,” said the project teaam.
“The main advantages include: faster assembly, dimensional precision, reduced waste on the construction site, a lighter structure, and lower carbon emissions.”
The company claimed that the building is carbon neutral.

Timber construction for tall buildings is gaining popularity across the world, with inroads into construction in North America and Europe. The current tallest timber structure in the world recently topped out in Australia.

items.titel: Even Elizabeth Holmes cried at the end of Pride & Prejudice.
items.anriss: Elizabeth Holmes, the chief executive officer and founder of Theranos, a health care technology company, listens as Deputy Secretary of Defense Ash Carter speaks at Stanford University in Palo Alto, Calif., April 17, 2013. (DoD photo by …

absaetze.t: The zeitgeist-y movie everyone is talking about right now is You Can See Everything, Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s meta-documentary about Thermos’s Elizabeth Holmes and her family. Holmes invited the filmmakers to document the weeks before she heads to prison for wire fraud; the result is profoundly strange and thought-provoking.

The press tour and chatter around the movie has been just as revealing and confounding. But one moment particularly caught my eye. It’s from a talk with Fielder and Oppenheim at the SCAD Savannah film festival. Oppenheim—who I feel is being overshadowed by Fielder, but has done equally great work, like Some Kind of Heaven, Spermworld, and Ren Faire—is talking about how he and Fielder were unclear what Holmes and her husband Billy Evans wanted out of this film project, and says this:

I remember early on, before we started shooting, Billy showed us a video—because he would sometimes video things on his phone—just of him and Elizabeth, like on a couch, and he’d be like, ‘Look at this moment,’ and it’d be a video of Elizabeth crying, and he’s like, ‘We just watched Pride & Prejudice. This is so good.’ So I was like, ‘Are these the type of moments that you are interested in? You know, what is the object of your guys’ inquiry with this?’
This kind of moment is exactly what the film is interested in: what are everyone’s motivations and intentions? What is real and what is a magic trick? How deep do the scams and manipulations go?

And now I’m also wondering, what about Austen’s story makes Elizabeth Holmes cry? Is she over-identifying with a fellow Elizabeth, a woman who secures a marriage to a man who is proud but ultimately good? Does she think Billy “We Are Charlie Kirk” Evans is like Darcy? Or not like Darcy? Is she struck by Austen’s assertion that a search for self actualization and self knowledge is attainable? That one doesn’t have to scam and deceive as a way to sublimate other, unexamined emotions?
Or is she just borne along by a good story, convinced and willing to invest (emotionally) after a well-performed pitch?
We will simply never know.

absaetze.t: “S’élevant (Rising)” (1962) was snatched from Gallery Ludorff's booth on November 8.
November 12, 2026 — 2 min read

German police are seeking answers about the theft of Hans (Jean) Arp's “S’élevant (Rising)” (1962) from Gallery Ludorff's booth at Art Cologne, which went missing from its plinth on the last day of the blue-chip fair on Sunday, November 8, between 4:55pm and 5:10pm.

Since the fair kicked off on November 5, Arp's work had been sitting atop a plinth at the Düsseldorf gallery's booth, sandwiched between two paintings by Ernst Wilhelm Nay. Four employees were at the stand on November 8 and immediately notified the North Rhine-Westphalia State Police upon noticing that the unbolted sculpture, which is valued at €145,000 (~$160,000), had gone missing. As it remains unclear who made off with the 28-centimeter-tall (~11 in) sculpture, police are seeking any information or photographs from visitors or staffers that could aid in the investigation.
